key_insight: Qwen-RobotWorld unifies embodied world modeling by using natural language as the action interface to predict future visual trajectories. It aims to model how a scene will evolve across robotics, driving, navigation, and human-to-robot transfer from current observations.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the lack of a single, scalable world model that can understand instructions and forecast physically plausible future states across multiple embodied settings. Existing systems are often task-specific and do not generalize well across domains or support reusable simulation and data generation.
method: Use language-conditioned video generation as a world model that maps current observations plus text instructions to future visual predictions.
Treat natural language as a unified control/action interface across different embodied tasks and environments.
Learn physically grounded trajectory prediction for diverse domains including manipulation, autonomous driving, indoor navigation, and human-to-robot transfer.
impact: This matters because it can reduce dependence on costly real-world data collection by generating synthetic training data and virtual rollouts. It also offers a more general framework for building and evaluating embodied AI systems across many tasks with one model.

paper_title: Qwen-RobotWorld Technical Report: Unifying Embodied World Modeling through Language-Conditioned Video Generation
paper_authors: Jie Zhang, Xiaoyue Chen, Anzhe Chen, Chenxu Lv, Deqing Li
